# Joint cap variations for common-orientation simplex fibers

These are finite-family differential lemmas. They do not assert separate
stationarity of individual fibers of a stationary mixed cap.

## 1. Exact joint gradient and Hessian

Let `T=conv(v_0,...,v_d)` be a simplex and let the positive fibers be
`K_z=t_z+s_z T`, `s_z>0`, at finitely many integer indices `z`. Simplices
with one common set of oriented facet normals have this form. Indeed
their `d+1` support numbers modulo the `d`-dimensional translation
subspace have only one degree of freedom, namely positive dilation.

Fix `y=(z_0,x_0)` and an ambient cap through it with normal `p=(a,u)`.
Its vertex values are

`c_{z,i}=a.(z-z_0)+u.(t_z+s_z v_i-x_0)`.

Let `P(c)=Pr(sum_i c_i E_i>=0)` for independent unit exponentials, and
let `w_z=s_z^d |T|`. Then its exact mass is `F(p)=sum_z w_z P(c_z)`.
Write `A_z` for the matrix with rows
`(z-z_0,t_z+s_z v_i-x_0)`. In a chamber where no vertex is on the cap
boundary, differentiation gives

`grad F=sum_z w_z A_z^T grad P(c_z)`,
`Hess F=sum_z w_z A_z^T Hess P(c_z) A_z`.                 (1)

Strict full and empty fibers contribute zero. For proper fibers the
derivatives of `P` are exactly the exponential size-bias and convolution
formulas in `candidate 8704554a92158bfc`. In
particular, for distinct vertex values,

`P_ij=(P_i-P_j)/(c_i-c_j)` for `i!=j`,
`Hess(P)c=-grad P`.

Equation (1) records the actual coupling: all fiber variations arise
from one vector `(delta a,delta u)`. It does not permit independent
variations of the separate margin vectors `c_z`.

## 2. A coherent descent when the fiber centroids form an affine selector

Assume `d>=2`, `z_0` is one of the positive fibers, and `u!=0`.
Normalize the reference simplex so `sum_i v_i=0`. Suppose

`t_z=x_0+A(z-z_0)`                                      (2)

for one real matrix `A`, so `y` is on the affine selector of fiber
centroids. The affine shear removing `A` preserves the integer base and
the continuous volume on each fiber; equivalently keep the original
coordinates and use the variation described below.

Put `b_i=u.v_i` and
`r_z=a.(z-z_0)+u.(t_z-x_0)`, so
`c_{z,i}=r_z+s_z b_i`. Thus vertex-value ordering is common to all
fibers. Let `i,j` index a largest and second-largest `b` value.

Assume every fiber is either strictly full, strictly empty, or properly
cut. In every properly cut fiber assume:

* at least two vertices are strictly included;
* its section centroid has barycentric coordinates at most `1/d` at
  the two vertices `i,j`.

Then this ambient cap is not a local minimum of mass through `y`.
In particular it suffices that every proper section centroid belongs to
the full central barycentric region. No individual section centroid is
assumed to equal `y` or its projection to that fiber.

Proof. Choose `delta u` with vertex values `+1` at `i`, `-1` at `j`,
and zero elsewhere. It exists because `sum v_i=0`, and the map from
continuous linear functionals to their vertex values has image exactly
the vectors whose coordinate sum is zero. Set

`delta a=-A^T delta u`.

By (2), the resulting common ambient variation leaves every `r_z`
unchanged and changes the margin vectors by

`delta c_{z,i}=s_z`, `delta c_{z,j}=-s_z`,
`delta c_{z,k}=0` otherwise.                             (3)

Both selected margins are strictly positive in each proper fiber,
because they are the two largest ones and that fiber has at least two
strictly included vertices. Let `f_z` be the density of
`sum_k c_{z,k} E_k` and set

`phi_z(c)=f_(V_z+cE)(0)/f_z(0)`, `psi_z=1/phi_z`, `c>0`.

The proved reciprocal-transform lemma says `psi_z` is convex,
`psi_z(0+)=1`, and `psi_z'(c)>0` wherever `psi_z(c)>=1`.
For any simplex section, not just one stationary in the full mixed
objective, its centroid coordinates satisfy

`phi_z(c_{z,k})=d lambda_{z,k}`.

This is the exponential size-bias/section-centroid identity. Thus both
selected values of `psi_z` are at least one.

If `b_i>b_j`, then `c_{z,i}>c_{z,j}`. Convexity makes `psi_z` strictly
increasing on their entire interval, and hence
`phi_z(c_{z,i})<phi_z(c_{z,j})`. The first variation of the mass in
direction (3) is therefore

`sum_(proper z) w_z s_z f_z(0)
 [phi_z(c_{z,i})-phi_z(c_{z,j})] <0`.                    (4)

If `b_i=b_j`, the first variation vanishes, but the exact repeated-value
Hessian formula gives second variation

`sum_(proper z) 2 w_z s_z^2 f_z(0) phi_z'(c_{z,i})<0`.   (5)

Here `phi_z'=-psi_z'/psi_z^2<0`. Strict full and empty fibers remain so
for sufficiently small variations and contribute nothing. Other zero
vertex margins of a proper fiber stay zero under (3), so the positive
pair differentiation remains valid. There is at least one proper fiber:
the center fiber contains its centroid `x_0` in its interior and `u!=0`.
Equations (4) or (5) prove the claim. QED.

The affine-centroid condition and the strict full/empty conditions are
explicit feasibility assumptions. Equation (1) alone does not supply
them for an arbitrary family of translated homothets.

## 3. A concave integer-tilt direction for one-excluded-vertex caps

The following lemma does not require common facet normals. Let every
positive fiber be a simplex of dimension `d>=2`. Suppose a cap through
`y=(z_0,x_0)` strictly includes all or none of each nonproper fiber, and
in each proper fiber it strictly excludes exactly one vertex and strictly
includes all its other vertices. If some proper fiber has `z!=z_0`,
the cap cannot be a local minimum in the full ambient normal family.

Proof. Hold the continuous normal fixed and vary the integer coefficient
by `t delta a`. In a proper fiber let `h_z>0` be minus the excluded
vertex value, and let

`D_z=product_(other vertices j) (c_{z,j}-c_{z,excluded})>0`.

All these differences stay fixed under integer-tilt variation. The
excluded simplex has exact relative volume
`[h_z-t delta a.(z-z_0)]^d/D_z`. Therefore

`d^2 F/dt^2 at 0
 =-d(d-1) sum_(proper z)
   [w_z h_z^(d-2)/D_z] [delta a.(z-z_0)]^2`.             (6)

Choose `delta a` not orthogonal to an off-center proper index. The
right side is strictly negative. Strict full/empty gaps preserve their
zero contributions locally. This excludes a local minimum. QED.

For triangular fibers, every proper cut with two strictly included
vertices has the form in this lemma. If only the center fiber is proper,
all other fibers are strictly full/empty, and the center's own
barycentric coordinates are at most `1/2`, stationarity reduces to that
single triangle; the proved single-simplex theorem again excludes a
local minimum with two included vertices. These are chamber statements;
supporting-facet contacts can invalidate their conclusion, as the exact
example in `candidate 52245e36c2630aa2` shows.
